title.narrative: Conflict Prevention and a Peaceful Election in 2012/13

description.narrative:
Kenya has been on a recovery path from experience of election violence experienced. As set in Agenda four, the reform processes has realized new laws passed in the form of a new constitution. The major setback is continued citizenry and voter apathy, lack of strong public engagement in the Constitution implementation processes and subsequent political processes including upcoming elections - this has become the major challenge in Kenya. The processes is further complicated by new electoral laws and electoral reforms as Kenya moves closer to the next general elections. The passivity of citizens will impact negatively on electoral reforms and validation of the election results.
Citizens and political aspirants are gearing up for elections based on the county system. As a result some counties are polarized as ethnic identity and perceptions are playing a major role in the quest for county leadership and political positions. This is an indication of high possibility of violence.
The project is focusing on these strategic areas in view of supporting free and fair elections; - Stronger public engagement in political processes towards 2012/13 elections - Working towards peaceful elections processes with an acceptable outcome in 2012/13
Governance and Democracy Programme within Catholic Justice and Peace Commission will anchor the project. The project will be carried out in six dioceses of Marsabit, Isiolo, Maralal, Mombasa and Malindi for community based activities. Some of the activities will include carrying out intensive civil campaigns, development of a simplified version for Constitutional Education during diocesan workshops and disseminating this information throughout the established church structures and communities. Election oberservers will be trained and a monitoring report shared with stakeholders. This is a twelve month project from May 2012 to May 2013.
